title: Left-Handed Transmission Lines for the Dynamical Casimir Effect
authors: Valentin E. Salari, Fernando C. Lombardo, Paula I. Villar
abstract: Left-handed (LH) superconducting transmission lines, built with series capacitors and shunt inductors instead of the series inductors and shunt capacitors of a conventional right-handed (RH) line, have a spectrum with a nonzero lower band edge and modes that become sparse at high frequencies. We study the dynamical Casimir effect in a LH line terminated by a flux-modulated SQUID and compare it with an RH line built from the same elements and with a long coplanar waveguide terminated by the same SQUID. We derive the quantum Hamiltonian and show that the coupling between two modes factorizes into their amplitudes at the SQUID. Together, the LH spectrum and the mode dependence of this coupling determine which modes are populated and how fast. With equal elements, the LH coupling grows with frequency and exceeds the RH one above a crossover pump frequency set by the cell inductance and capacitance, and only the LH line has resonances above the RH band edge. Pumping two modes at once lets a weakly coupled mode borrow coupling from a strongly coupled one, while crossings of resonance lines populate three or four modes without increasing the growth rate. Compared with the coplanar waveguide, the LH line has a similar coupling but keeps the created particles in the target mode, whereas the nearly equidistant waveguide spreads them over many pairs and needs more pump energy.
summary: This paper investigates the Dynamical Casimir Effect using superconducting transmission lines, contrasting left-handed (LH) and right-handed (RH) configurations. The key finding is that the LH line exhibits superior coupling characteristics at higher frequencies compared to the RH line. This work is significant for understanding how circuit geometry dictates quantum field dynamics in superconducting quantum devices.
main_problem: The study compares the Dynamical Casimir Effect (DCE) generated in Left-Handed (LH) versus Right-Handed (RH) superconducting transmission lines.
main_result: The LH line exhibits coupling that grows with frequency above a crossover point, possesses resonances above the RH band edge, and retains created particles in the target mode, unlike the RH line.
method: The authors derived the quantum Hamiltonian for both systems, analyzed the spectra, and compared the mode-dependent coupling constants.
model_or_system: The system involves superconducting transmission lines (LH: series capacitors/shunt inductors; RH: series inductors/shunt capacitors) terminated by a flux-modulated SQUID.
key_observables: Particle creation rate, inter-mode coupling constants, spectral features (band edges, resonances).
important_parameters: Pump frequency ($\Omega$), crossover pump frequency ($\Omega_c$), inductance ($L$), and capacitance ($C$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed for a finite number of unit cells ($N$) without taking the continuum limit.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows schematics for both LHST and RHST lines terminated by a SQUID.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian for both LH and RH circuits, analyzing their respective spectra and coupling terms, and finally comparing the resulting DCE particle creation rates and mode dynamics.
why_interesting: The comparison between LH and RH structures provides a concrete, tunable superconducting circuit model for studying non-standard quantum field dynamics, which is highly relevant to cavity QED and open quantum systems.
